prompts.prompt: Create a production game sprite ATLAS, 4 columns by 4 rows of 16 separate residential building plots. Reference image is STYLE AND CAMERA ONLY: keep its realistic materials, warm neutral concrete/brick, orthographic nearly top-down oblique camera facing north/front faces, visible roofs and south/front facades, and SQUARE axis-aligned ground plots. Do not reuse the 5x3 layout. New atlas is a mathematically regular FOUR BY FOUR grid with no gutters between equal square cells; each building and its complete square ground parcel fits inside its own cell with a 4 percent transparent margin. Exterior background and spaces between plots are truly transparent, no text or labels or borders. Every parcel faces exactly the same camera angle. Each column visibly increases building height/density, from left to right: column 1 low apartments (3-4 floors), column 2 midrise apartment blocks (6-8 floors), column 3 high-rise residential towers (15-20 floors), column 4 unmistakable tall residential SKYSCRAPERS (35-50 floors), with much smaller roofs relative to long visible window facades. Each row changes architecture while keeping the same density progression: row 1 modest brick housing, row 2 clean concrete residential slabs, row 3 modern glass-and-concrete apartments, row 4 luxury pale stone / glass condominiums with roof terraces. Each square plot has paving, small landscaping, entrances and physically plausible footprints. The high-rise/skyscraper columns MUST look dramatically taller than the low-rise columns; no low flat office blocks in the rightmost column. Daylight, high-end photorealistic city-builder assets matching the reference viewing direction, strong silhouettes at small sizes, no aerial perspective convergence. All sixteen whole square parcels remain contained in their respective equal-size atlas cells without overlapping neighbours. No streets on the parcels. Transparent background.

Keep the EXACT same four-by-four residential atlas: identical sixteen buildings, equal cell grid, square plot sizes, roof shapes, perspective, geometry, landscaping, materials, camera, and image composition. Change ONLY lighting to nighttime. Illuminate many of the actual individual facade windows warm golden yellow, with a natural occupied/unoccupied window pattern, subtle lit entrances and a little realistic spill on paths. Tall towers must have long columns of small warm lit windows. Do not create new windows, buildings, props, roads, labels, text, halos on the entire plot, or opaque background. Preserve the source alpha cutouts and all transparent gutters EXACTLY. Dark blue night ambience on unlit roofs and ground, retain clear structural detail. This is the matched night texture for the same game sprites; day/night images will crossfade and silhouettes must line up.

Create a production city-builder sprite atlas with TWO separate merged residential skyscraper complexes on a transparent canvas, using the attached image as CAMERA AND MATERIAL STYLE reference only. Strict layout: canvas aspect ratio THREE wide by TWO tall. Use a logical grid of THREE columns and TWO rows. Asset A occupies the top-left TWO grid squares as one complete rectangular ground parcel, aspect 2:1, horizontal footprint (six game tiles wide by three tiles deep). The bottom-left two grid squares are EMPTY TRANSPARENT. Asset B occupies the RIGHTMOST column across BOTH rows as one complete rectangular ground parcel, aspect1:2, vertical footprint (three game tiles wide by six tiles deep). Keep each asset completely inside its assigned rectangle with 4 percent transparent margin. No gutters, text, labels, ground outside parcels, or extra objects. Both complexes use the reference orthographic nearly top-down oblique camera, visible roofs and south/front faces, EXACT same viewing direction: do NOT rotate one image to make the vertical footprint. They are designed as naturally different horizontal and vertical site plans. Each merged complex is an impressive photorealistic pair/group of very tall 45-60-floor residential skyscrapers with long visible grids of individual facade windows, small clearly detailed rooftop mechanicals, a unified podium, landscaped central court and paths tying together the whole rectangular parcel. Rich pale stone and contemporary glass, slightly warm concrete, believable tall building depth matching a top-down SNES-style city map. These must be unmistakably tall residential towers, not low brown apartment blocks. Square-aligned rectangular footprints (no diamond or isometric rotated-ground shape), realistic materials compatible with the reference, neutral daylight. Preserve TRUE alpha transparency outside both parcels and throughout the unused lower-left part of the atlas.

Keep the EXACT same two residential tower complexes and atlas layout, at the same size and camera. Top-left horizontal complex occupies the upper-left two thirds of width and upper half of height. Right vertical complex occupies the rightmost third of width and full height. Lower-left unused area must remain completely TRANSPARENT. Preserve every roof shape, tower/podium/landscaping position and rectangular footprint precisely; do not redesign, rotate, mirror, or move any object. Change ONLY lighting to night, with numerous warm golden individual lit facade windows, selected unlit windows, gentle entrance and court lighting, and dark blue but visible roofs. Preserve true alpha transparency surrounding both parcels and in the large unused lower-left region; do not add grey backgrounds, fog, labels or text. The night image must match the day image's silhouettes and geometry for crossfade game animation.

A photorealistic city-builder game sprite ATLAS of TWENTY distinct COMMERCIAL building plots in an exact regular grid of FIVE columns by FOUR rows. Attached reference is material/camera/style only. Every equal grid cell is one whole SQUARE axis-aligned parcel; ground plots are never diamonds. Nearly top-down oblique orthographic camera, roofs and front/south facades visible, same direction in all cells, matching the reference game sprites. Do not mix side-on and top-down views. No perspective convergence, no labels, no text, no borders. Transparent background, transparent narrow gaps, each whole parcel fits within its own cell with a 3 percent margin. Across every row, the FIVE columns must visibly progress from low-density shops/retail buildings (one-two floors), to small office blocks (five floors), midrise offices (ten floors), tall office towers (twenty-five floors), and unmistakable commercial SKYSCRAPERS (fifty floors) with long visible window facades and small roofs. Four architecture/style rows: modest brick/stone shopping district; pale concrete office/business campus; contemporary blue glass offices; premium glass-and-stone corporate centre. Each density is a visually different building arrangement, not a mere recolour. All parcels square, full paving, entrances and modest landscaping, no streets or parked crowds outside parcels. Realistic high-end city-simulation building materials consistent with the reference. No logos or signage. Crisp recognisable silhouettes when scaled to small game tiles. Daylight.

Make a matching NIGHT LIGHTING variant of this exact game sprite atlas. Preserve image dimensions, grid layout, each building shape, camera angle, all roofs, facades, plot boundaries, transparency and empty spaces precisely. Do not add, move, rotate, replace or redesign anything. Change only lighting: dark blue nighttime ambience while retaining visible roof/structure detail; illuminate many existing individual facade windows with warm golden light, natural occupied/unoccupied window patterns, entrances, and a few realistic yard lights on industrial plots. No new buildings, no signs/text/labels, no broad yellow plot glow, no opaque backdrop. Match original silhouettes and geometry so day and night can crossfade. Keep TRUE alpha transparency outside the square plots and in gaps.

A production photorealistic city-builder sprite ATLAS with EIGHT different INDUSTRIAL building plots, exact regular FOUR columns by TWO rows of equal SQUARE cells. Attached image is STYLE/CAMERA reference only: consistent nearly top-down oblique orthographic camera, roofs and front/south facades, axis-aligned square plots (never diamonds), realistic concrete, brick and steel. Each whole parcel entirely inside its own cell with a 4 percent transparent margin. Background and gaps true transparency. No text, labels, borders or logos. In each row, columns progress visibly from small production plot, to medium factory, to large dense factory, to very dense large industrial complex. First row light manufacturing/warehousing: varied sheds, skylights, loading bays, small metal-working production halls. Second row heavy industry: varied brick/steel production halls, tanks, distillation towers, furnaces and smokestacks. Eight distinct layouts and silhouettes with increasing density across the four columns. Roof details, pipes, yards and machinery, small entrances, believable rectangular buildings, square whole parcels. No active smoke clouds obscuring the objects. No streets or stray objects outside plots. Same camera orientation on every building and same quality/material realism as the reference. Neutral daylight.
